title: Net 1 and Net 365 are exact to the day
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure work order 1, for a customer on the shop's own term due 1 day after the invoice date, and work order 2, for a customer on the shop's own term due 365 days after, are complete and ready to invoice.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1's Finance tab.
  2. Set Invoice Date to Oct 31, 2026.
  3. Set Invoice Date to Dec 31, 2026.
  4. Open work order 2's Finance tab.
  5. Set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  6. Set Invoice Date to Feb 1, 2028.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The invoice preview shows.

Step 2:

  • The Due date reads Nov 1, 2026 (Oct 31 + 1 day).

Step 3:

  • The Due date reads Jan 1, 2027 (Dec 31 + 1 day).

Step 4:

  • The invoice preview shows.

Step 5:

  • The Due date reads Oct 5, 2027 (365 days; February 2027 has 28 days, so a year is exactly 365).

Step 6:

  • The Due date reads Jan 31, 2029 (2028 has 366 days, so 365 days falls one day short of Feb 1).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R1: “A Net term (standard or the shop's own) is due that many days after the invoice date: an invoice dated Oct 5 on Net 30 is due Nov 4; on a shop's "Net 10" it is due Oct 15.”
  • Key Decisions: “Net terms run from 1 to 365 days.”
